_doc: THE MISFIT LEDGER (Palle, 2026-11-11: 'can we build a category or assemblage theory that is not restrictive?' ... 'yes, pilot the misfit ledger on the randomness floors'). PROPOSED, not authored: nothing here changes commons/modular/grammar.json, terms.json or the timeline. The grammar stays strict - a strict check is what makes a misfit visible - and this file is what happens to a misfit: it is FILED, not rejected and not quietly fixed. Each entry says which READING found it, what does not fit, how we know (STATUS), and one line: WHAT WOULD HAVE TO CHANGE for it to fit, and where that change would land. An entry may stay open for good: a singleton is allowed. A PROPOSAL is a change to the grammar (or a card, or a term's wording) that several entries ask for; it carries a TEST - the floors re-read with the change applied in memory: what it removes, what it creates - and it waits for Palle. An operation is real when several works need it and accepting it removes misfits without creating more. The readings are kept apart: where two disagree, both are recorded (`second`). Re-measure with `python tools/misfits.py --test`.

pilot.note: 95 works. Only 2 of them have a confirmed form today; the timeline, parts and words readings below are read WITH the forms proposed in that thread applied in memory, so their status is 'imagined' until the forms are confirmed. Floor numbers are the working tree's: the committed rooms.json has two floors fewer (other sessions' uncommitted insertions), so an entry names the map where it matters.

readings.timeline: the earned rule and the axis levels (tools/grammar.py check): a work may use an operation only after the card that introduces it
readings.parts: recurrence (doc/WORLD_UNITS.md, Recurrence first): which works descend from a part that three or more works share
readings.words: what the term formulas say that the grammar has no operation for: unknown call words, and joining words the reader skips
readings.eye: one photograph of each work against what its form says it wants to show (ada_run/robot_pilot/randomness/eye_*.json)
readings.body: rays on a 0.25 m grid and the Void's walker driven across (tools/probes/void_standable.gd)
readings.arrival: the floor from its spawn point (tools/void_arrival_worklist.py sorts boxes; the pictures and the walk decide)
readings.idea: each work's own statement (its @identity: essence, desire, truth), its history and its lineage, against what the floor lets a visitor do with it (Palle, 2026-11-12: 'what is the idea of this artifact and can it be expressed in a better way')

status.imagined: said by a proposed form, a plan or a box: nothing in the running tower has been asked
status.built: it is in the repo and loads; nobody has stood in front of it
status.observed: measured in the running tower: a photograph, a survey box, a ray, a walker's leg, the headset

lands_in.grammar: an operation, an alias or an axis level in commons/modular/grammar.json (Palle's)
lands_in.card: a card on a term: where an operation or a level is introduced
lands_in.timeline: a row's place or track in commons/data/artifact_timeline.json
lands_in.floor: a placement, a wall, a prop or a route in commons/void/rooms.json
lands_in.work: the work's own code or config
lands_in.reading: the instrument was wrong, not the work
lands_in.nowhere: nothing is proposed: it may stay as it is

entries.misfit: Four works give a value to every point of a surface (a photographed image, a field of chances, height = visits, height = accumulated mark) and none of them is noise. The only card that introduces `field` is the noise card on floor 92.
entries.would_change: `field` is introduced on the randomness floors by a card of its own, before the first of them; the noise card then adds only what noise adds (neighbours related).

entries.misfit: Ten works on floors 86-90 are made of noise, and the noise card stands on floor 92 (placed by hand on randompoint, the root card of the noise sequence).
entries.would_change: Either `field` is earned earlier (p1: the check is then satisfied, the works still use the PART noise before its card), or the noise card moves to the first noise work (tested: removes 15, creates 4 - three fields are still earlier, and the spine rule objects that a root card stands off its sequence's floors), or the ten works move to the noise floors (not tested: one of them is floor 90's ground).

second.says: Under p1 the timeline reading is satisfied and the parts reading is not: the check counts operations, not parts. Kept as a disagreement.

entries.misfit: env_one counts as using `field` only because its part cone_field is written `by(array(plastic_cone, 4 x 4), random: jitter, turn)` and the reader takes `by` for `field`. It is a throw, not a field.
entries.would_change: cone_field's formula says `random(...)`. Taking `by` out of the aliases of `field` instead was tested and is worse: it also stops standing_wave and disco_grid, two honest fields, from being read.

entries.misfit: sculpt_one uses `boolean` 74 floors before its card (bool_union, floor 161): its part noise_blobs is written `field(noise - t ∩ sphere)`.
entries.would_change: One work, so no operation is asked for. The formula means a threshold inside a sphere and could say `decide`; or the fault is left standing as a true early use.

entries.misfit: Two rows on the main track are furniture for reading: a wall of text and a 0.4 m document lying on the slab. Neither has a form and the eye calls both 'not visual'.
entries.would_change: They go to the environment track (an operation the timeline already has).

entries.misfit: Three entropy specimens with no draw in them (a chair, a cup at five moments, a chair behind five panes) stand outside every part.
entries.would_change: Nothing is proposed. They would join a part if `measure` had a second level - a count of the ways a thing could be - which is what floors 78-79 are about; the seven order-and-shuffle works beside them sit at measure:1. That level needs Palle's sentence, not a draft.

entries.misfit: Two works take chance from the world, not from a generator: the clock's measured frame intervals and the visitor's own movement. No part says 'measured'.
entries.would_change: A part 'the measured source' needs three. lava_entropy_wall and geiger_counter show a measured source but run on a generator, so today it is two that measure and two that depict. Not proposed.

entries.misfit: A graded tilt with no draw in it, on a floor of drawn rotations: it is the control, and nothing in its form says what it is the control OF.
entries.would_change: A way to say `A beside B`: two forms that differ in one thing (see m10).

entries.misfit: `exhibit(...)` is written in 16 term formulas (15 drafts and one canonical term) and the grammar has no operation and no alias for it. The canonical one, exhibit_cube, says 'staging, not a new principle' - and the drafts keep reaching for the word.
entries.would_change: `exhibit` is read as an existing operation (an alias of `association`: a label, a lamp, a screen name the work and change nothing the engine computes), or staging becomes an operation of its own.

entries.misfit: 12 term formulas join two forms with `beside` (throw beside field, a surface beside its noisy copy, order beside shuffle). The reader reads call syntax only, so the comparison - the thing these works are FOR - is not read at all.
entries.would_change: `A beside B` is read as an operation: two forms that differ in one thing, the difference is the reading.

entries.misfit: 31 term formulas put one thing `on` another (on quad, on field(noise ground)). Unread.
entries.would_change: Nothing is proposed. It reads as plain support; it is filed because the count is high and because 'on a ground' is the same relation as m12.

entries.misfit: 8 term formulas say 'ground' or 'what you stand on' in plain words (field_terrain: 'the surface is also what you stand on'). The grammar has `hand` - it fits a hand, it can be taken - and nothing for a surface that carries a body.
entries.would_change: An operation for ground: a surface a body can stand on and is moved by.

entries.misfit: Rays and the walker disagree. random_walk_128: rays find 81 m2 to stand on, the walker is stopped at the foot of its mound (first filed as 'stopped by its glass' - wrong: the glass room has two open doorways; corrected 2026-11-12 after reading the code). entropy_ruin: rays say walkable, the walker stops at its border. pheromone_terrain: rays read relief, the walker crosses a flat collider under the ridges.
entries.would_change: With an operation for ground a form can SAY which it is - ground, or a specimen under glass - and the disagreement becomes a statement. Per work: a collider that follows the ridges; the ruin may stay closed. random_walk_128 is settled (2026-11-12): a body on its growing lattice is boxed in between columns, so the lattice stands smaller in its room, the visitor stays on the plain around it, and the walk begins at the doorway.

second.says: All three photograph as terrain. The eye cannot tell ground from a picture of ground.

entries.would_change: A way up where the top is worth reaching (the walk-up on floor 90 is the pattern); otherwise nothing - a top you cannot reach is not a ground.

entries.misfit: Staging, arrival, folding a floor into another, a playground: the acts that made floors 85 and 90 readable are acts on a FLOOR, not on a form. They live in prose (doc/WORLD_UNITS.md) and in rooms.json (walls, props, routes, carriers); the grammar of forms cannot say one of them.

entries.would_change: A placement can say it is the floor's WELCOME - the work the arriving player is meant to stand at or on - and the sorter and the arranger leave it. Three floors have one; that it recurs is the reason to name it.

second.says: These are the three best arrivals of the sixteen floors. Each was composed from an idea of what the arriving body does - enter, operate, follow - not from boxes.

entries.misfit: random_edge_profile says 'the interior is free because somebody decided in advance where the ends would be'. Its floor held 48 placements of it, black from the spawn point, and nothing let a body meet the idea.
entries.would_change: The same idea at the scale of a body, from parts the tower has earned by then: two plank causeways from one table of draws, nothing refused beside the ends held. The 48 plates were not touched: whether they stay a field or become three (relief, plate, column) is Palle's.

entries.misfit: The first build of the causeway claimed that the lane with nothing refused cannot be walked. The tower's walker crossed both lanes: at five points a span and 0.28 m of variation the cliffs were small enough to ride over.
entries.would_change: Three points a span and 0.6 m of variation: the held lane is walked end to end, the other stops the walker inside its first span. The work's header keeps the failed measurement (`measured`).

entries.misfit: Read as code, not as a one-liner, random_edge_profile does one thing: it fixes two of five values and leaves the rest to chance. The same move builds forms the tower has already shown: a line (two fixed ends, a sampled route between), a catenary and a curtain (points pinned, the rest hangs), a pendulum, a standing wave, a point clamped to its bounds. The grammar has `tie` for one body holding another and no word for a form whose points are held while the rest is free.
entries.would_change: An operation for holding: some points of a form are fixed, the rest stays free. Then the profile and the causeway are the randomness instance of a part the tree already depends on, not two singletons.

entries.misfit: Floor Random_Gaussian shows the count seven ways - four sampler cabinets, a comparator, a paint canvas, a Galton board - and all of them are watched. Their code shares one idea: a shape appears that no single draw has, and the same randomness makes a different shape under each rule. Nothing let a body meet a shape.
entries.would_change: The same draws sorted into three plank walks (uniform, gaussian, exponential) rising toward the Galton board. Measured with the tower's walker: it reaches the top of the even walk and of the bell walk, and on the exponential one it is stopped at 0.67 m - the tail. A first build with one flat plank per draw failed: the walker cannot take a 5 cm riser, only a slope.

entries.misfit: The bridge from chance to noise - 'independent draws versus spatial correlation' - stood on floor Random_Space_Geometry as two 24 cm grids at chest height behind the room, and as two buttons of seeded_room that show one state at a time. The comparison has a meaning for legs that nothing let them try.
entries.would_change: Two grounds from one seed beside the arrival: heights drawn alone, and heights read off a field. Measured with the tower's walker: it crosses the related ground end to end (0.64 m of hill) and is stopped 0.3 m into the one drawn alone. The 24 cm model now stands at the pair. Also on this floor: random_transformations_geometric taken out of sculpt_one's footprint into the west bay (m19).

entries.misfit: pollock_painting_in_3d says a drip painting is the trace of a body moving through a random field with intention, and its own notes say the break was a posture: the canvas on the floor, the body walking round it. The only body was a cursor, on a 4 m canvas beside the spawn point.
entries.would_change: Where a room asks, a body walking on the floor canvas is the brush: the path is the visitor's, chance decides width, wobble and drops. The canvas lies 7.2 x 4.8 m where the player lands. Measured: the tower's walker crossed it and left a line the full width of the image. The view tool had photographed the canvas plain grey: it hid every CanvasLayer to remove the game's overlays, and so hid the painting's own layer inside the work - a fault of the reading, fixed the same day. Then, on Palle's word: open buckets stand on a 13.8 x 9.2 m canvas and the player paints by carrying one; the pipe walk became a playground maker that floors every square whose four corners exist (108 quads on five levels).

entries.misfit: Floor Random_Pheromone is about a channel: marks left in the ground enter the next walker's decision. It showed that as a 4.8 m model with a console whose back faced the arriving visitor, and read as code the live walk is switched off there (comparison mode). A body could look at the channel and press steps; it could not enter it.
entries.would_change: scent_trail_ground: 12 x 10 m of flat ground where the visitor is one more writer. Two records of every step, as the hall text already distinguishes them: scent (pink, fades, read by 120 blue walkers) and wear (pale, stays, read by the visitor). Predicted on the bench, then measured with the tower's walker: 5 % of the walkers on its line before, 45-53 % after three crossings; 25 s after it left the scent is down to the walkers' ceiling and the wear is still there. Refuted on the way: a ring does not hold them (65 % at 5 s, 8 % at 20 s), and a version whose diagonals looked further than straight ahead turned nobody onto a line met square on. The console model moved to the south-east and now faces the visitor.

entries.misfit: The hall text of Random_Pheromone (final.md) begins 'At the console' and never mentions a ground a body can walk; the first thing a visitor now sees from the spawn point is that ground, and the console is to the right, out of the first view. The text's own distinction - the history we see against the signal the walker reads - is what the ground shows, in other words (wear, scent). One clipboard on the floor still claims shortest paths, which the essay already contradicts.
entries.would_change: The essay's writer decides: one sentence that sends the reader onto the ground before or after the console, or the essay stays the console's and the ground speaks through its own board. Nothing was changed in the text.

entries.misfit: pheromone_terrain is a relief: height is where the walkers went. On the slab it was read from the side, at the height of its own ridges, and from the console. A relief is a map and no eye could get above it.
entries.would_change: On Palle's word the model lies over shaft B, a lid 4.8 m wide in a 6 m opening, and site_shaft_play_scaffold stands round the shaft: a plank ramp up, a deck of pink and blue quads 0.9 m out over the opening at 2 m, a slide down to the console. Measured with the tower's walker: up the ramp to 2.0 m, along the deck over the opening, down the slide; the lid carries a body; the gap north of it still takes a body down the shaft. The scaffold is a reusable piece (origin at a shaft's centre). A first caption board on the rail hid what it named; the line now lies on the deck.

entries.misfit: Floor Random_Space gives the body a ground of independent draws. Its main work, the noise mixer, is an 80 cm picture on a plinth: read as code, a sum of four terms - one wave at 1, 2, 4 and 8 times the frequency, each half as tall. The hall text asks the reader to reduce the layers to one and add them back. Nothing let a body meet a term.
entries.would_change: layer_sum_islands in the west bay: five islands from the mixer's own seed, wave, offsets and colour ramp - four hold one layer each, the fifth their sum; the cut faces of the fifth show the four lying on each other. Measured with the tower's walker: feet within 4 cm of the drawn height at the same three spots on all five; the four heights add up to the fifth; the sum crossed on two of three lines when each finer layer weighs 0.5 and on one of three at 0.7. The hall text and the mixer on its plinth are untouched; the essay does not mention the islands.

entries.misfit: The playground round shaft B was built by hand twice: first a ramp, deck and slide from loose tubes (m35), then the pipe walk with ramps of my own. The tower already has a maker: commons/modular/places compiles a place written ((y), (width, length), (depth)) into the workshop's own fixed parts, and an artifact goes in as the place's activity. A hand-built scaffold is a second construction inventory, invisible to the lab editor and the workbench.
entries.would_change: Palle: 'use the playground maker and make a basin and fit the artifact, place in the shaft b at level 0' and 'find the principal of playground making'. The pheromone model is now the activity of a kit pool ((1), (6, 6), (1)) in a playground_spec_hall over shaft B; a 6 x 6 m pool is exactly the shaft, so its floor closes the opening at level 0. pheromone_terrain learned to fit a slot. Measured with the tower's walker: up the kit's ramp to the rim, down the descent onto the model, out again. The hand-built scaffold of m35 is removed from the repo. Not covered: the other body-scale works of this pass (causeway, stairs, ground pair, islands) are built from loose boards too; they are works with an idea of their own, but their decks and ramps could be kit places.

entries.misfit: The biome vocabulary gives four of the growth sequences words the biome object does not draw: cellularautomata has `rule` and `grow`, fractals `recurse`, noise `field`, proceduralgeneration `constrain`, and biome_object at those stages is the same picture as at randomness (benched at six cells, seed 7: 151 drawn things at noise, cellularautomata and fractals alike). Only lsystems changes it (`tree`, `creature`). So a biome box on a CA, fractal or procedural-generation floor would show nothing its floor has taught; the pilot boxes stand only on L-system floors for that reason.
entries.would_change: Either the object learns to show those words (the cover spreading by a rule at cellularautomata, the tree's branching depth at fractals, a placement that has to satisfy a constraint at proceduralgeneration), or the vocabulary says plainly that they are known and not yet drawn. A change inside biome_object, whose lineage is shared: a proposal, not started.

entries.misfit: The Boolean_Verbs yard (2026-11-13): twenty construction prefabs made as isosurfaces stand on the two wings and round the shafts - a tunnel, a crossing and a dome to walk into, a wall with three cuts sized for a body, a hand and a ball, a sieve, a basin, a gutter ramp, a mould and its cast, a hump bridge, a die, a gyroid screen, a stile, a mound, stones, a pipe tee, a spiral ramp, a funnel, a chute and a boulder - each with collision, each face coloured by the operation that made it. The hall text says its exhibits 'have not enabled collision ... Keep that difference with you when the objects become architecture', and 'we could make the new faces announce another origin'. Both now happen in the same room and the text does not know it; it still speaks of three objects on one line. Hall text follows the current map, and the map moved. Since then two side slabs carry the yard further out: north, the Random Boolean Carving's six carvings and the dome; west, the passes - a 16 x 5 x 9 m box carved from the inside out (a spiral room round a pillar, a grid corridor, a random walk whose floor climbs to 0.9 m and drops, a sine, branches that leave through the roof as light), its skin giving each pass its own colour and lighting the walls where two met. The text has no word for a difference a body walks through for minutes. And a third, east, where the visitor performs the verbs instead of meeting them made: a small block on a stand and a big one to walk into, in which a visitor can paint their own cave - aim and hold, difference carves and union builds, as a sphere, a cube or a cylinder, each stroke in its own colour (boolean_cave).
entries.would_change: The text keeps its three verbs on the centre line and gains the yard where it says the objects become architecture: the cut faces in orange are the 'other origin' it imagines, and the stile (connected, not passable) is its own 'being connected and being smooth are different accomplishments' built for a body. The passes belong where the text says the objects become architecture: the verb difference, met as a building one is inside of, its plan readable off its walls. The caves belong where the text hands the verbs to the reader: there the reader holds them. Not done here: the hall texts are not the pass's to edit.

entries.misfit: Shader_11_QueerRubber got the wardrobe as rooms on 2026-11-14 (Palle, shown the boolean cave's skins lining the corridors of their comfort test: 'add this the or a map'): two side slabs, east and west, seven tunnels each - latex, PVC, rubber, studded leather, chrome, glitter, sequin; holographic foil, fishnet, the pride rainbow, neon, pearl, velvet, drag - each a 2.4 x 2.6 x 7.6 m room lined in one skin, in a black latex shell named on its lintel. The hall's text asks what a surface answers to and finds the lamps (without their shadows), the eye's angle, the clock and a painted coordinate. The tunnels add an answer it does not have: a wardrobe skin answers to WORLD position - its grain, studs, net, bands and discs are laid in metres of the world, not on a painted coordinate - so a body walking a tunnel finds the pattern held still on the walls, where the hall's leather would carry its grain with its own turning. Its glints are taken from the head's centre, its mirrors from each eye, and its clock loops every 30 s (the TIME rollover; the ring's rainbow, a tenth of a cycle a second, is three whole turns of it, so it never leaps). The text also does not mention that four of its materials (leather, oil-slick latex, pop plastic as PVC, velvet) are now rooms beside the boards that show them on bodies.
entries.would_change: The text gains the two installed blocks where it lists what a surface answers to: world position as a fifth answer, and the difference between a skin looked at and a skin stood in (the captions say it in one line). Whether pop plastic and the wardrobe's PVC are one material in the text's words is the text's call. Not done here: final.md and tutorial.md are not this pass's to change.

The text does not mention a bridge, because in the museum the cave stood on a floor.

entries.misfit: AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulation (Palle, 2026-11-15: keep going until the end). The hall text is about one workshop: a body whose joints and connections a hand can move and reroute, an assembly that finds its places, another body that falls, furniture. It ends on what that body cannot do: 'The catalogue beside it has spare parts. This body cannot yet take one. Perhaps the next desire is another joint, another connection, more room.' In the tower the workshop stood nine metres from the arrival and three table pieces the text does not mention stood in a row across the arrival, two in columns. The pass moved the workshop to the middle of the floor and the table pieces aside. And one work the text does not mention: joint_more, on the west wing - the same body drawn on the floor, which a visitor's feet can add to.
entries.would_change: 'This body cannot yet take one' is still true of the workshop's body; the floor figure can take up to twelve. 'The useful question is which operation would let that desire take form' has one answer standing: add, with the neighbour either given by a rule or chosen by holding a joint. 'A list of positions would miss what happened' is now two lines on a stand. The text's body is kept for the final hall when changed; the floor figure keeps nothing between visits. The text does not mention the three table pieces or the lattice room on this floor.

entries.misfit: PostCrisis_Synthesis (Palle, 2026-11-15: keep going until the end). The hall text is about two standing bodies and a ledger: 'Beyond the ledger, an amber body holds the last pose kept in the Assembly Laboratory. The blue body beside it holds the starting arrangement.' In the tower the bodies stood eight metres from the arrival, and five works the text does not mention stood in a row along the south edge behind the arriving visitor: two with their backs turned, two in columns, one past the slab. The pass brought the bodies and the ledger toward the arrival and set the others round them. And one work the text does not mention: two_arrivals, north of the bodies - a record that keeps the path of a walk, two alternatives of it, and a note.
entries.would_change: 'What would you want the record to keep next? The path of the hand ... Another version of the pose ... A note might keep the reason' now has all three standing, for a walk and not for the hand: a path, the earlier walk beside the latest, and a note in the hall's own three words (carefully, reluctantly, with delight). 'Increasing the precision of its final coordinates would not recover the movement' is a walk kept without its path, which stays without one. The amber bay is empty in the tower until a pose is kept on the floor above; the text says that emptiness belongs to the work. The text does not mention the formula, the sphere, the table of words, the synthesis piece or the text panel on this floor.

entries.misfit: Russell_Paradox, gone back to (Palle, 2026-11-16: go back to floors 189, 190 and 195; use what we learn from the rest of the sequences in how we can build examples). The hall text walks from the workbench to works it places by words: 'Nearby, braces close around themselves', 'Deeper in the hall, boxes hold the same demand', a barber, a lamp. In the tower those four works stood in the four corner columns of the wings, fourteen metres from the arrival and inside the concrete, and the plaque stood a metre past the north edge. The pass brought the braces and the boxes to the west of the middle and the barber and the lamp to the east, in the text's order, and built the two examples the argument had only written down: in_and_out (the two buttons as two gates on one corridor) and fence_beyond (cell 6 as a yard with one thing always outside it). What does not fit the text: the hall says 'Your hand has somewhere to go; the proposed set does not' and the floor now says it of a body walking out of a corridor; and the text's cell 6 stops at one filter of four members, while the yard repeats the filter three times and ends in tape. Neither is in the text.
entries.would_change: If the hall text is revised for the tower: one sentence after the two buttons that the same question can be walked north-east of the middle, and one after cell 6 that the filter can be run again on the wider collection, each time with one thing outside. The words 'Nearby' and 'Deeper in the hall' are true of the floor again. Not done: the yard's fourth stage is tape because the slab has no room for a fourth fence; a headset trial of both works; the DNA picture sweep of the two axes.

entries.misfit: Godel_Incompleteness, gone back to (Palle, 2026-11-16: go back to floors 189, 190 and 195; use what we learn from the rest of the sequences in how we can build examples). The hall text places its works by words: 'the machine across the hall', 'Four smaller works between the machine and the exit', 'By the exit stands a framed picture', and of the tower 'A pulse climbs it and finds the gap again on every level'. In the tower eight of those works stood inside columns along the two long edges, and the incompleteness tower floated three metres past the south edge, behind the arriving visitor. The pass put the machine east of the sorter and the plaque across the shaft from it beside the word PROVABLE, the four checking works in a row on the north-east, the picture south of shaft A, which is the way down, and the tower on the slab inside a stair built round it (gap_moves_up). What does not fit the text: there is no exit on a tower floor, so 'between the machine and the exit' has no place to be true, and the four works stand together instead; 'At your smaller bench' has no bench here, the checking station does that work; and the stair lets a visitor add a sentence by standing on a plate, which the text warns about in its own way ('Try replacing G with a personal conviction. What is missing?') - the reading board says a conviction is not a plank.
entries.would_change: If the hall text is revised for the tower: 'the exit' becomes the shaft that is the way down; 'between the machine and the exit' becomes a row to the north-east; and after 'Adding the sentence moves the gap up. It does not close it.' one sentence that the visitor can walk it: three sets of planks, four landings, and the next sentence straight above the first. Not done: the works still float a metre above the slab as the transfer left them (height 1), with nothing under them; a headset trial of the stair, whose fourth landing is two metres up; the DNA picture sweep of the axis.

entries.misfit: Euclid_Parallel, gone back to (Palle, 2026-11-16: keep going with Euclid and Escher). The hall text speaks of a tutorial at a table: 'Draw the gold line through C in the direction of AB', 'Move C, hide the guide, bring it back', 'Now bring the three corners into one straight row. The face disappears and the reading is withheld.' None of that table is on the tower floor; the floor had the small triangle whose labels say sixty, and the lane where the fifth postulate is walked. The pass built the table's construction at body size (three_wedges): the visitor is C, the guide can be tilted and hidden, and a row of three positions is refused under a stated tolerance. What does not fit the text: the text never tilts the guide - it moves C and hides the line - and the floor's tilted setting is the pass's own addition, there because a filled line through C looked like evidence and is none; and the text's refusal is of a face that disappears, while the floor withholds wedges and numbers under ten degrees, a threshold chosen here.
entries.would_change: If the hall text is revised for the tower: 'the tutorial' and 'the table' become the field south of the shaft, where the reader is C; and one sentence after 'a parallel through a vertex lets the angles be compared along a straight line' that any line through C is filled, and that the parallel's work is the equality with the corners at A and B. Not done: Escher_Impossible was looked at and left as it stands - its cardboard stairwell was taken off the floor on Palle's word when the roof stair replaced it, and that record ('built, not placed') is a decision, not a gap; a headset trial; the DNA picture sweep of the axis.

proposals.title: `field` before noise
proposals.in_words: A card that introduces `field` at the first field of the randomness floors: image = field(sample, a value at every point). A value at every point of a surface, drawn and not yet related to its neighbours. Noise then adds one thing: neighbours agree.

card.formula: image = field(sample, a value at every point)
card.motive: a drawn value at every point of a surface: a picture nobody arranged
card.said: drafted 2026-11-11 from the misfit ledger (m01, m02) - not yet his words

tested_instead.what: the noise card lands at the first noise work (mushrooms, floor 86)

proposals.forecloses: `field` no longer arrives with noise. Both cards would raise chance to level 2; if p1 is accepted the chance axis wants a level between 'at every point' and 'kept by a rule' for 'neighbours related'. The card's host is the first USER (the lava wall, floor 77), not the clearest statement (floor 83, which builds nothing in the tower: m18).

proposals.title: cone_field is a throw
proposals.in_words: cone_field = random(array(plastic_cone, 4 x 4), jitter, turn) - the same sentence without `by`.

term_expr.expr: random(array(plastic_cone, 4 × 4), jitter, turn) = cone_field — a prefab field; walk between them

tested_instead.what: `by` is no longer an alias of `field`

proposals.forecloses: Nothing. It is a canonical term's wording, so it is Palle's to change.

proposals.title: `exhibit` is read
proposals.in_words: exhibit(form) is association: a label, a lamp, a screen. It names and shows the work; the engine computes nothing new.
proposals.forecloses: Staging cannot be earned or counted: it disappears into `association`. If staging should be something a floor EARNS (as floors 0-11 do with 17 route stops each), it wants its own operation instead - see m21.

proposals.title: `beside`: a comparison is an operation
proposals.needed_by: 12 terms; 4 works on these floors, the control on floor 83, and the drafted order-and-shuffle card (7 works)
proposals.in_words: compare(A, B): two forms that differ in one thing - the difference is the reading. Written `A beside B`.

axis_level.level: a difference: two forms that differ in one thing

operation.name: compare
operation.adds: two forms that differ in one thing: the difference is the reading

test.note: Not testable in the order check: the reader reads call syntax, and `beside` is written between two forms. Accepting it means the reader learns one infix word.

proposals.forecloses: A comparison becomes something a work must have earned: the first `beside` in the tower would need the card. Sorting (`sort`) already reads parts by a measure; the line between sorting many and comparing two has to be drawn by Palle.

proposals.title: ground: it fits a foot
proposals.needed_by: 8 terms; on these floors 20 works and props with standable area, 7 of them walked
proposals.in_words: ground(surface): a surface a body can stand on and is moved by. `hand` says it fits a hand; this says it fits a foot. A fourth level on the body axis.

axis_level.level: a foot: it can be stood on

operation.name: ground
operation.adds: it fits a foot: a body can stand on it and is moved by its shape

test.note: Built and observed on floor 90 (random_space fitted to its slot, the walk-up lookout; e2fb5df86). The order check is untouched until a form says `ground(...)`.

proposals.forecloses: A terrain under glass must then choose: ground or specimen. The working name collides with commons/modular/ground_profile.gd (another session: a footprint for the electrical mesh); Palle names it.

proposals.title: hold: some points fixed, the rest free
proposals.needed_by: 7 forms across five sequences: line_vs_trace, catenary, curtain, pendulum, standing_wave, clipped_point, pinned_random_profile
proposals.in_words: hold(form, where): the named points keep their place; everything between them is free to hang, to wave or to be drawn. What a boundary is for.

operation.name: hold
operation.adds: some points are fixed: the rest is free between them

test.note: Counted by reading the formulas: seven say that points are held, pinned, fixed or clamped while the rest moves. Not testable in the order check until a form says hold(...).

proposals.forecloses: It sits close to `tie` (one body holds another). If both exist, a pinned rope end is a tie to the world and a held value is a hold; Palle draws the line or folds them into one.
